justification: Critical: corrects how three SEPP (Housing) 2021 granny-flat rules are stored (wrong clause and wrong meaning for lot size, lot width, parking) and adds the engine the customer-facing granny-flat tools will read. Production data migration in two steps.

pre_impl.existing_data: housing_sepp_standards: 45 rows, 12 secondary_dwelling. Rows 44 (min_lot_size 450 '53(1)(b)'), 34 (min_lot_width 12 'Schedule 1, Part 2'), 35 (parking 0 'Part 3, Division 2') do not match the SEPP (Housing) 2021 in force (11 September 2026), checked against legislation.nsw.gov.au 2026-10-08.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The 450 m2 figure is s 53(2)(a), a non-discretionary site-area standard for detached secondary dwellings on the DA path; the CDC path (Sch 1 cl 2(1)(b)) sets a road frontage of 12/15/18 m by lot-area band; no numeric parking standard exists. The conveyancing loader does float(numeric_value), so wording rows with no number would crash it; the brief lists unknown standard types as additional standards.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Additive: new columns (083, applied) and 7 new rows (084, applied only after this code deploys). Old rows 34/35/44 stay until consumers switch in the next PR. Generic readers now skip approval_pathway rows.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A database error loading the rules returns named failures (UNAVAILABLE), never an empty rule set; a missing lot fact returns UNKNOWN for that path.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend change in this PR. The engine returns per-path dicts: outcome, reason, clause, quote and legislation link for each rule used.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Until consumers switch (next PR) customers see the current behaviour; after 084 the existing readers return exactly what they return today, proved in a rolled-back transaction (45 and 39 rows, identical eligibility view).

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_secondary_dwelling_paths.py tests/test_provenance_check.py tests/test_legislation_monitor_no_silent_pass.py tests/test_dockerfile_monitors_imports.py -q -o addopts=
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any fail-closed guard is removed: six mutations (stale rule accepted, value not checked against quote, band gaps accepted, unmeasured frontage = PASS, DA always MEETS, missing lot area guessed) each made 1-4 tests fail.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed 2026-10-08: 119 passed. Mutations each caught: six on the engine (1-4 failures each) and four on the cross-review fixes (frontage accepts m2: 1; path tag unchecked: 2; zone ignored: 3; excluded zone accepted: 1). Provenance: 9/9 rules traced to their own clause in the law in force, run on the Fly server from its whitelisted IP; linking the 12 m rule to the 15 m clause gave 8/9 with that rule named. 9/9 migration quotes word-for-word in the live law. Round 3 (cross-review): Decimal lot area treated as missing, missing path rules passing the weekly check, and an undelivered alert reported as sent were each fixed and each mutation-caught (1 failure each); 141 passed.

functions.name: validate_rules
functions.input: housing_sepp_standards rows tagged with an approval pathway, each carrying its quote of the law
functions.output: validated per-path rules with ordered lot-area bands, or a tuple of named failures for UNAVAILABLE
functions.if_none: No rows or any missing rule yields named failures; callers report UNAVAILABLE and evaluate nothing.

functions.name: evaluate_cdc
functions.input: validated rules plus lot area, frontage range at the building line and battle-axe status
functions.output: CDC road-frontage outcome PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN with the clause, quote and link used
functions.if_none: Any missing or invalid input returns UNKNOWN with the missing fact named.

functions.name: evaluate_da
functions.input: validated rules plus lot area and whether the granny flat is detached from the dwelling
functions.output: DA site-area outcome MEETS, BELOW, NOT_APPLICABLE or UNKNOWN, with the law's own note when below
functions.if_none: Missing detached status or lot area returns UNKNOWN with the reason.

values.value: No regulatory numbers in code; thresholds and band limits are database values checked against each row's own quote
values.source: housing_sepp_standards rows inserted by migration 084, quoted from the SEPP (Housing) 2021 in force
values.read_at: each request, via load_rules in services/secondary_dwelling_paths.py
values.if_missing: Any missing, stale or self-inconsistent rule returns UNAVAILABLE with named failures.

queries.where_clause: development_type = 'secondary_dwelling' AND approval_pathway IS NOT NULL

queries.purpose: generic standards loader excludes path rules

break_it.scenario: A path rule is edited so its number no longer matches the quote of the law it carries
break_it.what_happens: validate_rules names the rule and the engine returns UNAVAILABLE instead of using the edited number

break_it.scenario: The lot-area bands are edited so a lot size falls in no band or in two bands
break_it.what_happens: validate_rules reports a gap or overlap and no CDC answer is produced for any lot

break_it.scenario: Lot area, frontage or detached status is missing for a property being assessed
break_it.what_happens: That path returns UNKNOWN naming the missing fact; nothing is guessed or treated as a pass

break_it.scenario: A lot under the DA site area is reported to the customer as not allowed
break_it.what_happens: It is reported as BELOW with the law's own note that non-compliance does not prevent consent

break_it.scenario: The load path rules query fails because the database is unreachable or errors
break_it.what_happens: load_rules returns 'rules query failed' after a rollback and the caller reports UNAVAILABLE
break_it.how: exception mapped to a named failure

break_it.scenario: The generic standards loader receives the new wording rows that carry no number
break_it.what_happens: It filters approval_pathway IS NULL so the rows never reach float(); 45 and 39 rows with them present
break_it.repro: insert migration 084 inside a transaction, call fetch_sepp_housing_standards and the eligibility query, then roll back

break_it.scenario: The eligibility engine query picks up path rules and changes which clause a form cites
break_it.what_happens: It filters approval_pathway IS NULL; the rolled-back check showed its view identical to before
break_it.repro: insert migration 084 inside a transaction, call fetch_sepp_housing_standards and the eligibility query, then roll back

break_it.scenario: A stored rule's link points to a clause other than the one its words come from
break_it.what_happens: The weekly provenance check reports the rule and clause, exits 1 and sends a Telegram alert
break_it.how: quote must sit inside the anchored clause

break_it.scenario: The law is amended so a quoted clause no longer exists or no longer says the same words
break_it.what_happens: The next weekly run names every affected rule and alerts; nothing passes silently
break_it.how: anchor existence and quote-in-clause checks against the live page
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_provenance_check.py -q -o addopts= -k 'anchor or changed'

break_it.scenario: The weekly provenance check cannot fetch the law or finds no rules to check at all
break_it.what_happens: Each is a named problem, the run exits 1 and alerts; an empty check is never reported as all traced
break_it.how: fetch failure and empty result are failures
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_provenance_check.py -q -o addopts= -k 'fetch or no_rules'

break_it.scenario: A frontage threshold is changed to a lot-area figure that also appears in its quote, such as 900
break_it.what_happens: Rejected: frontage values must match metres and site-area values must match square metres
break_it.how: unit-specific matching plus unit column check (cross-review finding 1)

break_it.scenario: A property in a zone outside a path's scope, such as R5 for CDC or E4 for both, is evaluated
break_it.what_happens: That path returns NOT_APPLICABLE; a non-standard zone code returns UNKNOWN; a missing zone returns UNKNOWN
break_it.how: per-path zone-scope rules quoted from s 49, s 50 and s 54(1)(a)
